title: Classes suspended in NCR, 37 other areas; WFH allowed in gov’t offices

passages: MANILA – Malacañang suspended classes at all levels in Metro Manila and 37 provinces on Thursday due to the combined effects of the southwest monsoon (habagat) enhanced by Tropical Storms Dante and Emong.
The suspension was issued through Memorandum Circular (MC) No. 91 signed by Executive Secretary Lucas Bersamin on Wednesday.
Local government units (LGUs) outside the listed areas may declare class or work suspensions based on prevailing conditions.

passages: Malacañang has announced the suspension of work in government offices and classes at all levels in the following areas due to the expected heavy rainfall that will be brought about by Super Typhoon Nando and the southwest monsoon.

These are Metro Manila, Abra, Antique, Apayao, Bataan, Batanes, Batangas, Benguet, Bulacan, Cagayan, Cavite, Ifugao, Ilocos Norte, Ilocos Sur, Isabela, Kalinga, La Union, Laguna, Mountain Province, Nueva Ecija, Nueva Vizcaya, Occidental Mindoro, Oriental Mindoro, Pampanga, Pangasinan, Palawan, Romblon, Rizal, Tarlac, and Zambales.

title: Metro Cebu LGUs declare suspension of classes due to inclement weather

passages: Four local government units (LGUs) in Metro Cebu suspended in-person classes on Thursday, July 17, 2025 due to inclement weather brought about by the southwest monsoon (Habagat) that dumped intense rains and inundated areas on July 16, 2025.

After deliberating with Department of Education (DepEd) Superintendent, Dr. Arden Monisit, face-to-face classes in all levels in Talisay City were suspended on Thursday, July 17, 2025, according to Mayor Gerald Anthony Gullas.
As for private schools and the Talisay City College, the discretion to cancel classes has been entrusted to their respective school heads, Gullas added.

All levels for public schools in Lapu-Lapu City were suspended "in light of the enhanced southwest monsoon (Habagat) intensified by Tropical Depression Crising and the issuance of the Orange Rainfall warning from state weather bureau PAGASA," Mayor Cindi King-Chan said in an announcement on her official social media page.
"For private schools, the suspension of classes shall be left to the sound discretion of the school management. Please check the announcements from your respective schools," Chan added.
Further, as recommended by appropriate offices due to the unfavorable weather forecast from PAGASA, all levels both public and private schools in Mandaue City were suspended on July 17, 2025.

Moreover, due to expected continuous rainfall that may lead to flooding, and in consideration of everyone's safety, all schools at all levels in Cebu City were advised to adopt asynchronous and/or modular delivery of classes, according to a public announcement made by Mayor Nestor Archival on July 17, 2025.

Through Archival's official social media page, and the Cebu City Public Information Office, the announcement directed schools to "implement early dismissal of students and personnel, if face-to-face classes have already started."
The announcement is in effect until further notice, the advisory added.

title: DepEd activates 4H protocol as Habagat disrupts classes

passages: The Department of Education (DepEd) has activated its 4H emergency learning protocol as heavy rains brought by the Southwest Monsoon, or Habagat, disrupted classes in Metro Manila and several provinces.
Under the protocol, schools may suspend, ease, adjust or resume learning activities depending on safety conditions, learner readiness and available resources.

The protocol is laid out under Memorandum Circular No. 123 issued by the Office of the President, which directed the use of alternative learning modes in affected areas on Monday unless otherwise ordered by local chief executives.

"Hinto" applies when conditions are unsafe or when the safety, protection or basic needs of learners are at risk. Academic activities are temporarily suspended so schools and communities can prioritize safety, emergency response and essential support.

DepEd said schools that have shifted to asynchronous or other alternative learning modes because of the current rains may classify these arrangements as Hinay, provided that learners and teachers remain safe and learning requirements are adjusted to the situation.

title: Over 6.5M learners affected by class suspensions due to Maymay, Habagat

passages: More than 6.5 million learners were affected by in-person class suspensions in eight regions amid the combined effects of Tropical Cyclone Maymay and the Southwest Monsoon or Habagat, according to the Department of Education (DepEd).

As of 8 a.m. on Monday, August 10, the Education Department recorded a total of 6,517,252 learners and 288,967 personnel covered by in-person class suspensions involving 10,029 public schools across 61 school divisions in eight regions.

The highest number of schools with suspended in-person classes was recorded in Central Luzon (Region III) with 3,546 schools, followed by the Ilocos Region (Region I) with 2,428 and Cordillera Administrative Region (CAR) with 1,842.
The National Capital Region (NCR) had 827 affected schools, followed by Calabarzon (Region IV-A) with 623, Mimaropa (Region IV-B) with 608, Region II with 92, and Region VI with 63.

title: Verbena now over Sulu Sea; Signal No. 1 up over 13 areas
TD Verbena dampens Caraga; travels, classes suspended

passages: BUTUAN CITY – Most provinces in the Caraga Region experienced moderate to heavy rains early Monday morning, brought by Tropical Depression (TD) Verbena.
As rains continue to dampen the region, Philippine Coast Guard stations have temporarily suspended sea travel, while local government units (LGUs) have ordered the suspension of classes.
In Surigao del Norte, Gov. Robert Lydon Barbers said the Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council has issued a localized suspension of classes.
In Agusan del Norte, work at the provincial capitol and classes in both private and public schools were also suspended on Monday to ensure the safety of personnel amid severe weather conditions.

In Dinagat Islands, the LGUs also issued advisories to suspend classes in both public and private schools and advised residents, especially those in coastal areas, to stay alert and monitor the current weather conditions.
In Tandag City, Surigao del Sur, Mayor Roxanne Pimentel has ordered the suspension of face-to-face classes at all levels in public and private schools.
In Agusan del Sur, classes were also suspended in Loreto, Prosperidad, Talacogon, La Paz, Bayugan City, Esperanza, San Francisco, and San Luis. (PNA)

passages: Classes at all levels, both public and private, and work in schools of Kawayan Districts I and II, Municipality of Kawayan, Province of Biliran are suspended due to Tropical Depression Ada, effective Thursday afternoon, January 15, 2026, until lifted.
This was announced by Vice Mayor Jake Espina with an attached Executive Order (EO) and shared on Biliran Province page on Facebook.
Classes in the Province of Northern Samar will be suspended on Friday, January 16.
By noontime on January 15, Governor Harris Ongchuan ordered the suspension of classes at all levels in Northern Samar due to TD Ada.

In terms of suspension, DepEd clarifies that there is no automatic suspension of classes due to extreme heat under its current policy. However, local chief executives may declare class suspensions in affected areas.

title: Some schools shift to online classes amid transport strike March 24-26, 2025

passages: Classes will be held online instead of face-to-face in some schools from March 24 to 26, 2025 as transport group MANIBELA conducts a strike .

Adamson University : Synchronous online classes in all levels on March 24. Campus will be open for students and faculty members who may wish to use the facilities in their holding of online classes. All offices will also be open for onsite transactions.

Ateneo de Manila University : For Higher Education, Undergraduate and Graduate Levels (SOH, GBSEALD, JGSOM, SOSE, RGLSOSS) on March 24 to 26: In general, shift to online (synchronous or asynchronous) learning mode. Labs and other academic activities that need to be onsite may be especially arranged between instructors and students.
Centro Escolar University : Classes in all CEU campuses will shift to online for Monday. March 24. The midterm exams are rescheduled to March 26 to 29, 2025.
Colegio de San Juan de Letran : Synchronous online classes for all levels will be held on March 24. All offices will operate on a skeletal workforce.

De La Salle Araneta University : Classes for both the Integrated School (IS) and Tertiary Education Department (TED) will shift to online mode on March 24. Office operations and council meetings of administrators will proceed onsite as scheduled.

De La Salle University : Senior high school, undergraduate, and graduate classes at its Manila and Laguna campuses would be conducted online from March 24 to 26. Despite the shift, both campuses would remain open. Work at the Manila and Laguna campuses would also transition to a work-from-home setup, except for essential personnel in facilities, campus services, libraries, enrollment services, and finance required for campus operations.
Far Eastern University : Teaching and learning at FEU Manila and Makati will be conducted online on March 24. Library services will be available and office will be open for transactions.
Malayan High School of Science : Classes in all levels would shift to a synchronous online mode on March 24.
Manila Central University : All classes for Monday, March 24 will shift to online.

Mapua University : Senior high school classes in both the Intramuros and Makati campuses will shift to synchronous online mode on March 24. Summer term enrollment for undergraduate students on March 24 will proceed fully online as originally scheduled. For in-person transactions, the Admissions, Treasury, and Registrar’s Offices will be operating on a skeletal workforce.

Pamantasan ng Lungsod ng Maynila : Face-to-face (F2F) classes at all levels will shift to an online modality on March 24. The suspension does not apply to students engaged in clerkships, internships, RLE, OJT, and thesis defenses, which will proceed as scheduled. All university offices will remain open, and regular work operations will continue as scheduled.

Philippine Women's University : PWU-JASMS Manila classes will shift to online on Monday, March 24, while the planned sportsfest and fair at PWU-JASMS QC shall proceed as scheduled. Classes in PWU Taft Campus shall continue on synchronous online modality as scheduled. Work operations in all PWU and PWU-JASMS Campuses shall proceed as scheduled. Students who are processing their applications and enrollment may do so either in-person or online via www.pwu.edu.ph.
School of the Holy Spirit of Quezon City : regular online learning on March 24; shift to online learning on March 25
University of Perpetual Help System DALTA - Las Piñas : All classes for Monday, March 24 will shift to online or asynchronous. University offices will remain open for on-site transactions.

University of the Philippines - Diliman : Faculty members are encouraged to shift to remote or asynchronous modes of learning from March 24 to 26. For scheduled exams and other projects, faculty members in consultation with their students may opt to conduct such activities face-to-face.
University of Santo Tomas : UST will implement its "Enriched Virtual Mode of Instruction" and remote work arrangements on March 24, 2025.

In Bulacan, Governor Daniel Fernando also announced that alternative learning modalities will be used by public and private schools for all levels from March 24 to 26 as a response to the transport strike.

title: Manila suspends afternoon F2F classes Friday

passages: MANILA – The Manila City local government suspended face-to-face (F2F) afternoon classes in public schools on Friday due to the scorching heat.
In an advisory, the Manila Public Information Office (MPIO) said there would be no classes in the afternoon, from preschool to high school, including senior high school.

“To ensure that students will have a safe and balanced education amidst the persistent rise in temperature, face-to-face afternoon classes are suspended, from preschool to high school (including senior high school), in public schools in the city of Manila, tomorrow, March 7, 2025, Friday,” it said.
There will be face-to-face morning classes in all levels in public and private schools.
However, it is leaving to private schools the decision to suspend face-to-face classes.
“Private schools and higher educational institutions may suspend afternoon face-to-face classes at their own discretion,” it said.

title: Mga suspendidong klase sa Miyerkoles, Nov. 12, 2025

passages: Sa Facebook post ni Nueva Vizcaya Governor Jose Gambito nitong Martes, inihayag niya na walang pasok sa lahat ng antas ng paaralan-- pribado at pampubliko—sa buong lalawigan dahil sa marami pang kalsada ang hindi madaanan at mga lugar na hindi mapuntahan.

Sa hiwalay na pahayag sa FB post ni Tuguegarao, Cagayan Mayor Maila Ting Que, ipinaalam niya na wala ring pasok sa mga paaralan sa lahat ng antas, kabilang ang Law, Medicine, at Graduate Studies, face-to-face man o online, gayundin sa lahat ng government offices, para sa pinamumunuan niyang lungsod.

Suspendido naman mula sa Miyerkules (Nov.12) hanggang Biyernes (Nov. 14)  ang face to face classes sa lahat ng antas sa bayan ng Hinigaran sa Negros Occidental. Hinikayat ni Mayor Mary Grace Arceo ang mga paaralan na magpatupad ng alternative mode of learnings gaya ng modular.

Wala rin munang face to face classes sa Daycare hanggang Senior Highschool sa bayan ng Basista, Pangasinan mula November 12 hanggang 14. Hinikayat din ang mga paaralan na magpatupad ng modular distance learning.

Sa Binmaley, Pangasinan, suspendido ang klase sa pampublikong mga paaralan sa lahat ng antas sa Miyerkoles, "to allow the assessment of the safety and structural integrity of school buildings and vicinities by the Municipal Engineering Office and respective school heads."
Suspendido rin ang mga klase sa Aparri, Cagayan, sa lahat ng antas, pribado at pampublikong paaralan sa Miyekoles.
Nagdeklara ang lokal na pamahalaan ng Solana, Cagayan na walang pasok sa lahat ng antas ng paaralan, pribado at publiko sa Miyerkoles.

title: PBBM, Angara nag-abot ng tulong sa Cebu matapos ang lindol

passages: Batay sa ulat ng Department of Education (DepEd) noong Oktubre 1 ng alas-11 ng gabi, nasa 5,587 na silid-aralan ang may bahagyang pinsala, 803 ang may malubhang pinsala, at 1,187 naman ang tuluyang nasira sa mga paaralan sa Cebu. Higit 19,000 na mag-aaral at 950 guro at non-teaching personnel ang apektado.

Matapos ang beripikasyon mula sa mga field office, ilalabas ang opisyal na listahan para sa joint validation ng DepEd at Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) upang matukoy ang halaga ng rekonstruksyon. Tiniyak ng Kagawaran na agad na ilalaan ang pondo para sa maayos ang mga nasirang gusali.

Siniguro din ni Angara sa mga magulang at guro na magpapatuloy ang edukasyon matapos ang mga agarang hakbang, at binigyang-diin na pangunahing gagamitin ang modular learning bilang pinakamainam na paraan para sa mga komunidad na may nasirang silid-aralan o limitado ang koneksyon sa internet.

Upang mabawasan ang nawalang araw ng klase, na tinatayang aabot sa halos isang buwan sa pinakamalubhang naapektuhan, maglalagay ang DepEd ng Temporary Learning Spaces (TLS) sa Bogo at mga karatig-bayan ng Cebu. Uunahin dito ang mga batang nasa early grades upang masimulan agad ang limitadong face-to-face classes.

BOGO CITY, Cebu, 2 Oktubre 2025 – Bumisita si Pangulong Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr., Kalihim ng Edukasyon Sonny Angara, at iba pang opisyal ng pambansang pamahalaan nitong Huwebes sa Bogo, Cebu upang maghatid ng agarang tulong at suriin ang pinsala ng 6.9-magnitude na lindol na sumira sa libo-libong silid-aralan at komunidad sa hilagang Cebu.

title: Sarangani LGU extends class suspension, modified work post magnitude 6.6 earthquake

passages: Sarangani Governor Rogelio Pacquiao has directed the extension of the suspension of face-to-face classes and alternative work arrangements to a few days for further assessment and validation of structures after another strong earthquake hit the province last week.

In Executive Order No. 39, series of 2026, Pacquiao said that with the magnitude 6.6 earthquake that struck on June 26, 2026 "highlights the continuing seismic activity affective the Province and necessitates the further assessment, reassessment, validation and certification of the structural integrity of government buildings, and school facilities and other public infrastructure by the appropriate authorities.
He added that only after these processes are accomplished will regular government work and face-to-face classes resume.

Pacquiao acknowledged that the province has gradually transitioned to normal operations since a magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck on June 8, 2026 but structures have to undergo assessment and validation, and the issuance of safety clearance in order to protect the people.
The E.O. extends an earlier order that stated regular work and classes are to resume on July 1, 2026 to July 15, 2026.

Notwithstanding the suspension of classes, the governor said, teachers, school heads, and personnel may physically report to their respective schools provided that these were cleared by the Municipal Engineer's office and approval of the School Division head. — BAP GMA News

title: Negros Oriental suspends classes on Aug. 7, 2026 due to sore eyes cases

passages: Negros Oriental Governor Governor Manuel Sagarbarria has suspended classes in the province on Friday, August 7, 2026, to stop the spread of conjunctivitis or sore eyes.
Classes are suspended in all levels.

In Executive Order No. 50, the governor said the Integrated Provincial Health Office recommended the suspension of classes owing to the reported increase in the number of cases of sore eyes in several areas of the province.

In the same EO, Sagarbarria directed school heads, administrators, and officials of both public and private schools to utilize the day "to undertake appropriate cleaning, disinfection, and sanitation measures within their respective campuses and facilities, particularly classrooms, offices, comfort rooms, clinics, handrails, desks, chairs, learning equipment, and other high-contact areas."

title: Pangasinan PDRRMO sets guidelines on class suspension due to heat

passages: To provide clearer guidelines on suspending classes due to extreme heat, the Pangasinan Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (PDRRMC) has issued a memorandum outlining specific temperature thresholds.
This after several schools in the province have suspended classes as the heat index continues to rise, reaching an average of 42°C over the past three days.

"Kapag ang forecasted heat index ng PAGASA ay 45 degree Celsius or below, ang local chief executive ang may karapatan na mag-suspend ng classes o mag-shift sa alternative delivery mode of instruction," Assistant DRRM Officer Avenix Arenas said.
If the forecasted heat index reaches 46°C to 51°C, all public schools are required to implement the Alternative Delivery Mode (ADM) of instruction.
If the heat index exceeds 52°C, class suspensions will be automatic.
The Schools Division Office I of Pangasinan has adopted these measures.
However, according to Sherry Lyn Orjalo, SMN-DRRM of SDO I Pangasinan, schools must still wait for official suspension announcements.

"In DepEd order, walang automatic suspension, nakasalalay ito sa mga LCE and our school heads. Pagdating sa class suspension, hinihintay nila yung issuance kung magkakaroon ng suspension of classes," she said.
As of March 20, 2025, 10 towns under SDO-I have suspended classes due to the extreme heat: Bayambang, Malasiqui, Anda, Sual, Burgos, Basista, Calasiao, Sta. Barbara, Labrador, and Urbiztondo.
For private schools, class suspensions or shifting to ADM will depend on their policies and the heat index forecast from PAGASA.
announced_by: Pangasinan Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (PDRRMC)

title: New protocols issued on class suspension in Iloilo City due to heat index

passages: The Local Government Unit of Iloilo City issued Executive Order (EO) Number 24 on the establishment of guidelines and new protocols in the suspension of face-to-face classes.
Schools heads, administrators, and university presidents are given the option to suspend in-person classes once the forecast heat index in the city reaches 40°Celsius.
Cancellation of in-person classes will be based on the 5 p.m. heat index advisory of state weather bureau PAGASA on the day prior to the regular school day.
Adjustment to class schedules may start early to be able to finish by noontime, wherein classes could shift to the alternative mode in the afternoon.

School heads are given the discretion to shift to Alternative Delivery Mode (ADM) of instruction; however when the forecast heat index reaches 42°Celsius, in-person classes are suspended automatically to be able to shift to ADM.
The Iloilo City Government urged school administrators and university presidents to adopt the ADM.

It was learned that the Iloilo City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (CDRRMO) recommended the new threshold of 40°Celsius in determining the suspension of face-to-face classes based on PAGASA's 5 p.m. heat index advisory.
The EO signed by Iloilo City Mayor Jerry Treñas took effectivity on March 9, 2025.
announced_by: Local Government Unit of Iloilo City

title: QC gov’t updates guidelines for class suspension due to weather, disaster

passages: The Quezon City Government has issued a memorandum updating the localized guidelines for class suspensions due to inclement weather, extreme heat, earthquakes, and poor air quality.
QC Mayor Joy Belmonte released Memorandum Circular No. 3 Series of 2025, which aligns the local government unit's protocols with the Department of Education's order.
TCWS No. 1 : classes in public Child Development Centers and Kindergarten will be automatically suspended.
TCWS No. 2: public Child Development Centers, Kindergarten, and Grades 1 to 10.
TCWS No. 3: all public and private schools at all levels will be suspended.

The QC government also allows classes to be suspended in public Child Development Centers, Kindergarten, Grades 1 to 12, and the Alternative Learning System (ALS) during Orange and Red Rainfall Warnings.

Under the updated guidelines, the QC Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (QCDRRMC) is also authorized to declared localized class suspensions for specific public schools if PAGASA has not issued weather-related warnings.

For extreme heat conditions, public school classes in Child Development Centers, Kindergarten, Grades 1 to 12, and ALS will be suspended if the iRISE UP system forecasts a heat index of 42°C or higher.
The QC government allows the higher education institutions and private schools to decide on their class suspensions due to extreme heat.
According to the QC government, announcements are generally made at 5:30 PM the day before.
For earthquakes, all public school classes, including ALS, will be suspended in the event of an Intensity VI or higher.

Automatic suspension will be implemented in public schools from Child Development Centers to Grade 12 and ALS when the Quezon City Air Quality Monitoring Network reaches Alert Level 3, which occurs when 50% or more monitoring sites register air quality at Very Unhealthy, Acutely Unhealthy, or Emergency Levels.
Should the DENR-EMB reports an AQI Emergency Level, where PM 2.5 levels reach 91 µg/m³ (micrograms per cubic meter), all public and private schools at all levels will be suspended.
The local government units said announcements will be made no later than 4:00 AM on the day of suspension.
In cases of sudden extreme weather changes, suspensions will be declared no later than 10:00 AM.

Schools in Don Marcelino were urged to shift to alternative learning methods.

Tomas and  members of the EDSA Ortigas Consortium of Schools (EDSOR Consortium) namely, the Immaculate Conception Academy, La Salle Greenhills, Saint Pedro Poveda College, and Xavier School.
In a separate statement, De La Salle Philippines said all of its schools will also suspend classes and work on February 25.

title: DepEd NCR suspends F2F classes for Monday and Tuesday, Oct. 13-14, 2025

passages: The Department of Education — National Capital Region on Sunday has suspended face-to-face classes (F2F) in all public schools in Metro Manila on Oct. 13 and 14 to give way to disinfection and sanitation amid increasing cases of influenza-like illnesses.
In an advisory on Sunday night, DepEd NCR also cited the need to conduct building inspections following recent powerful earthquakes that hit different parts of the country.
The F2F suspension is to give way for the disinfection, sanitation, and building inspection of public schools in Metro Manila.
Public schools were told to implement alternative delivery modalities, such as online or modular instruction, "to avoid disruption of learning."

During the two-day F2F suspension, public schools will conduct cleaning and disinfection of classrooms and common areas and carry out structural and safety inspections of school buildings and facilities.

The advisory – signed by DepEd NCR Director Jocelyn Andaya – also stressed earthquake preparedness and response procedures, such as strengthened coordination with division engineers and local government units for inspection and mitigation actions.
The advisory also "highly encouraged" private schools to "observe and conduct these measures."

Earlier , some LGUs in Metro Manila declared class or F2F suspensions due to rising flu-like illnesses while other LGUs in Mindanao declared class suspensions due to continuing assessment  of the impact of recent earthquakes. — JMA/KG GMA Integrated News

title: WALANG PASOK: Classes, gov't work suspended in Davao, VisMin areas after magnitude-7.4 earthquake

passages: LIVE UPDATES: Davao Oriental earthquake (Oct. 10, 2025)

Local governments in Davao Region and parts of Visayas and Mindanao ordered the immediate suspension of classes and government work on Friday, October 10, following a powerful magnitude-7.4 earthquake that struck off the coast of Manay, Davao Oriental.

The Davao City government announced the suspension of classes in all levels, both in public and private schools, to allow authorities to promptly assess the safety of infrastructure and facilities in the metropolis.

"In view of the recent earthquake and to give way to the conduct of rapid damage assessment of infrastructures and facilities, classes in all levels, public and private educational institutions, in Davao City are hereby suspended immediately," the city government said in an advisory.
In neighboring Davao Oriental, Governor Generoso town also suspended classes and government work.

"Classes at all levels and work in national and local government offices within the Municipality of Governor Generoso are suspended today, Friday, 10 October 2025, due to the 7.6-magnitude earthquake," the order read.
Davao de Oro also announced the immediate suspension of work and classes except for frontline offices.

Meanwhile, the Office of Civil Defense (OCD) in Soccsksargen (Region XII) has announced multiple suspensions in the region covering General Santos City, Sultan Kudarat, South Cotabato, and areas in the provinces of Cotabato and Sarangani.

title: Floods reported in Luzon, Mindanao amid heavy rains

passages: Several areas in Luzon and Mindanao experienced flooding following the heavy downpour Tuesday, according to reports on GMA Integrated News’ Unang Balita.

A total of 97,274 people or 31,106 families in Luzon were affected by Tropical Cyclone Bising and the Southwest Monsoon or Habagat, the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council said Wednesday.
In its report, the NDRRMC said the affected population was reported in the Ilocos Region, Central Luzon, and Cordillera Administrative Region (CAR).
Classes in 247 areas and work schedules in 36 areas were suspended.
On July 4, a low pressure area inside the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR) developed into Tropical Depression Bising.
On July 6, Bising as a typhoon re-entered PAR.

title: School in Leyte suspends work, classes due to flooding

passages: A university in Baybay City, Province of Leyte has suspended work and classes due to heavy rains and flooding that affected parts of the main campus and nearby barangays.

Visayas State University (VSU) cancelled work and classes on Wednesday, August 27, 2025, after heavy rains triggered flooding in parts of the main campus and nearby barangays, forcing the evacuation of around 500 students.

“As announced via OP Memorandum Circular No. 220 s. 2025, all work and classes in VSU Main Campus are suspended until 12:00 noon of today, August 27, 2025, to allow affected dormitory occupants, workers, and students residing nearby to recover. Work and classes will resume at 1:00 p.m. today should weather conditions improve,” according to a post on Amaranth, the official student media organization of VSU.
announced_by: Amaranth, the official student media organization of VSU

title: Cebu town suspends F2F classes in 5 schools due to security threat

passages: The Municipality of Consolacion in Cebu has suspended face-to-face classes starting on Monday, August 3, 2026, following a security threat.

“In response to circulating online safety threats directed at local schools, the Municipal Government of Consolacion, Cebu, has suspended in-person classes for affected schools starting August 3, 2026, shifting them to modular/distance learning,” the town said in a statement.
- Consolacion NHS
- San Narciso School
- Tayud NHS (including Tayud ES)
- Tolotolo NHS (including Tolotolo ES)
- Tugbongan NHS (including Tugbongan ES)
The classes were suspended to allow authorities to investigate the incident thoroughly. Face-to-face classes will remain suspended until further notice, the town said.
The schools have been instructed to transition immediately to modular learning or alternative distance learning "to ensure academic continuity without compromising student safety."

Meanwhile, Talisay City Mayor Gerald Anthony Gullas said schools in the city are believed to be included as targets in the threat but the online posts only mentioned acronyms and did not identify any school by its full name. Because of this, the city did not impose a citywise class suspension order.

"After consultation with our police authorities and concerned agencies, the City Government will not impose a citywide suspension of classes at this time, as there is currently no verified information indicating a specific or credible threat directed at all schools in Talisay City," Gullas said.
One school, however, has decided to suspend face-to-face classes as a precautionary measure and Gullas said he respected and supported the decision.

In Cagayan de Oro City in Mindanao, the barangay where the Lapasan National High School is located recommended that the school suspend its in-person classes on August 3, 2026 also due to a security threat.

"The safety of learners and school personnel must remain the highest priority. Until the threat has been fully assessed and appropriate security measures have been implemented by the Philippine National Police (PNP) and other concerned agencies, it is prudent to adopt preventive measures to avert any possible harm," reads the memorandum Barangay Captain Julito Ogsimer sent to the principal of the high school.
announced_by: Talisay City Mayor Gerald Anthony Gullas
